assumptions.A1_ae_onset: an adverse event's onset day is uniform over the patient's reporting window (first dose to 30 days after the last dose): registries report cumulative incidence, not onset times
assumptions.A2_ae_grade: a serious adverse event is recorded at grade 3 (the lowest grade consistent with seriousness for most CTCAE terms); a non-serious event at grade 1 or 2 with equal probability; registries report seriousness, not grade
assumptions.A3_ae_resolution: a grade 1-2 event resolves by the next scheduled visit after onset; a grade 3 or higher event by the second: resolution is detected at visits
assumptions.A4_relatedness: adverse events generated by the safety model are treated as related to study treatment when a dose modification rule requires relatedness
assumptions.A5_lab_value_in_grade: during a laboratory-type adverse event, the laboratory value is drawn uniformly within that grade's CTCAE v5 range; outside events the baseline is carried forward
assumptions.A6_withdrawal_timing: a withdrawal (subject decision, loss to follow-up, physician decision) occurs at a uniformly distributed time over the patient's on-study period; its probability is from registry disposition
assumptions.A7_progression_exponential: when progression-free survival comes from a reported median only, progression times are exponential with that median
assumptions.A8_resume_same_dose: after a hold whose resume instruction the compiler could not type, treatment resumes at the current dose level
assumptions.A9_supportive_care_given: supportive care and prophylaxis are given as the protocol requires, so an adverse event that occurs is one that occurred despite them
assumptions.A10_normal_baseline_labs: laboratory values are within normal limits at baseline (patients met the protocol's organ function criteria); rules for patients abnormal at baseline are not applied
assumptions.A11_grade3_clinically_significant: an adverse event of grade 3 or higher is clinically significant where a rule requires it
assumptions.A12_reference_limits: laboratory reference limits (LLN: neutrophils 2.0, platelets 150, white cells 4.0 x10^9/L; hemoglobin 12.0 g/dL) are typical adult values; laboratories set their own
assumptions.A13_screening_day: the screening visit takes place at the start of the protocol's screening window
assumptions.A14_ae_discontinuation: beyond the protocol's own dose-modification rules, a patient stops treatment for an adverse event with the registry participant-flow probability, at a uniform time over planned treatment; a stop triggered by a protocol rule first takes precedence
assumptions.A15_death_timing: death in the study period has the registry participant-flow probability and occurs at a uniform time over the simulated horizon (registry flow periods span treatment and follow-up)
assumptions.A16_unknown_criteria_calibrated: eligibility criteria the generated patients cannot answer pass independently, with one probability chosen so that the eligible share matches the registry screen pass rate
assumptions.A17_standard_3_plus_3: when the protocol's escalation table cannot be compiled, the standard 3+3 table is simulated
assumptions.A18_participation_years: with no stated censoring rate, the registry study-period withdrawal share is spread over 2 years
assumptions.A22_short_participation: with no treatment cycles, participation ends after the last planned administration plus a 30-day reporting window, and the registry's whole-trial exit shares are scaled by that duration over a year
assumptions.A23_cr_share: when no complete-response input exists, complete responses are 15% of responses
assumptions.A24_tumour_dynamics: response depth is uniform within its category band, nadir is reached by the second assessment, progression is independent of response depth, and 35% of progressions are by a new lesion
assumptions.A25_recist_defaults: when the protocol compiles no response thresholds, RECIST 1.1 is used (PR 30% decrease, PD 20% and 5 mm increase)
assumptions.A26_post_progression_survival: death follows progression: post-progression survival is exponential with median equal to the arm's overall-survival input minus its progression median (at least 1 month; 12 months without an OS input); a patient who never progresses does not die of the disease within follow-up
assumptions.A27_subgroup_prevalence_equal: a protocol subgroup factor whose levels no registry baseline table (nor the protocol) reports is split equally across its stated levels
assumptions.A28_prognostic_effects: a subgroup effect from registry results by subgroup is prognostic: the same in every arm, multiplicative on the progression hazard and the response odds, independent across factors, and centred on the arm's patient mix so each arm's overall rate is unchanged
assumptions.A21_day1_dosing: an agent whose dosing days the protocol does not state is given on day 1 of each cycle
assumptions.A20_assessment_lag: with no stated time point or treatment length, the primary assessment is 6 months after entry
assumptions.A19_unnamed_arm_is_comparator: an arm that names no anticancer agent is the comparator: it receives the regimen of the arms without the investigational agent (the agent given in the most arms)
